routing_overall.conclusion: On 5 of 23 assertions the configurations differ at all; all 5 favour the candidate, and no assertion regressed against the baseline. 18 assertions are non-discriminating and prove nothing about the skill. The candidate's margin comes from finding playbooks an unaided session does not find (R1, R5, R7, R10) and from answering with an ordered sequence where no single playbook fits (R6).

discovery_overall.conclusion: No over-activation on any stated non-activation condition, including the two that matter most — a named playbook (T5) and a vault lifecycle operation (T6). One positive miss: T4 describes retrospective's domain without using the word 'retro', and the session went to the framebook instead. Activation appears to depend on the task reusing the playbook's own vocabulary.

limitations: One run per cell. Variance untested; no reliability claim follows from any single cell.
The old configuration covers only 4 of 11 cases, so old-versus-candidate attribution is partial.

Activation measured by self-report plus fingerprints, not harness instrumentation. Three candidate runs self-reported 'none' while displaying manifest-specific reasoning, so activation counts are a floor, not an exact figure.

Competing skills were present in every configuration by design (issues-to-roadmap, ndv-flow, and the rest of the user's skill set). They won activation in R3, R4 and the baseline R10. Routing outcomes therefore reflect a contested skill environment, not this skill in isolation.
The read-only prompt constraint makes every session more likely to describe a procedure than to start one, which inflates the baseline's apparent route-awareness and compresses the measured gap.
Case selection is adversarial toward the pre-revision skill by construction; the baseline column is the only guard against that, and it is a single run per case.
Only OpenCode discovery was exercised. The embedded manifest's portability rationale remains untested on any other harness.
No cost measurement; the skill's token overhead at load time is unmeasured.
Revision 2 of the plan discarded six earlier baseline runs after one of them committed a 141k-line deletion to the repo. Those runs are not graded and the incident is recorded in results.md.
lifecycle_decision: Supports draft -> validated. Documented outcome exists, the candidate beats the unaided baseline on every assertion where they differ, no regression, no over-activation. Does not support vetted: R2 and R3 fail, one discovery positive is missed, n=1 per cell, and promotion to vetted additionally requires a validated -> vetted transition that this run cannot authorise.
